name: Helm
summary: A Kubernetes package manager that renders chart templates from values, applies the resulting resource set through the Kubernetes API, and records versioned release state for upgrades and rollback.

features.name: Chart template and values composition
features.description: Helm combines chart templates, chart metadata, dependencies, and layered values into rendered Kubernetes manifests.
features.costs: Template scope, value precedence, and dependency interactions can make rendered output difficult to reason about

features.name: Versioned release state and history
features.description: Helm treats an installed chart as a named release and stores release revisions through a configurable storage driver, enabling upgrade history and rollback operations.
features.benefits: Provides an inspectable revision trail and recovery point
features.costs: Release storage consumes cluster state and rollback correctness depends on compatible manifests and live resources

features.name: Client and library boundary over Kubernetes API
features.description: The Helm client handles user-facing chart and repository workflows while the Helm library performs install, upgrade, and uninstall operations through Kubernetes API clients.
features.benefits: Allows other callers to reuse Helm operation logic
features.costs: Kubernetes API availability, permissions, and server-side behavior remain deployment dependencies

mathematical_views.question: How do chart dependencies, templates, values, and rendered resources compose into an installable manifest set?
assumptions: Chart dependencies form an acyclic or otherwise resolvable composition graph
Values are scoped inputs and template evaluation is modeled as a deterministic transformation for a fixed environment
The view does not infer semantic validity of every rendered Kubernetes resource

mathematical_views.question: How does a named release move through install, upgrade, history, and rollback states?
assumptions: Each operation produces or selects a release revision
Stored release records are treated as the history observed by Helm
The model does not claim rollback restores arbitrary external side effects

mathematical_views.question: Which Helm client/library operations cross into Kubernetes API resource management?
assumptions: Rendered manifests are the boundary objects sent to Kubernetes
The API server is modeled as an external stateful vertex
The view abstracts individual Kubernetes controllers

costs: Template indirection and value precedence increase review burden
History storage and resource drift complicate recovery

benefits: Reusable library operations over a standard API
costs: Cluster permissions and API availability constrain operations
